_comment: Assumptions for the Rotterdam textile-to-rPET Series A plan. All amounts in €k (thousands of euros). Every field cites a register ID (F=fact, A=assumption, E=inference, T=to be confirmed, S=source). Opex/headcount categories must use the model's internal category keys (销售费用=Selling, 管理费用=G&A, 研发费用=R&D, 其他费用=Other, 营业成本=COGS/production labour) — the English tables map them automatically.

downside.label: Downside: volume -15% (Line 1 commissioning slips ~6 months and offtake converts more slowly, R-01/R-02), price -5% (virgin PET at or below €1,000/t and flake imports, R-03), unit cost +4% (feedstock competition as EPR-funded sorting scales, R-04), opex +3%

upside.label: Upside: volume +8% (faster Line 2 utilisation as separate collection volumes grow), price +5% (PPWR/EPR demand pull and certified-content premium), unit cost -3% (negative-value feedstock fractions)

scenarios.rationale: Multipliers derived from the risk matrix (chapter 13): downside combines the probability-medium-or-higher risks R-01 to R-04 occurring together; upside only includes mechanisms with a regulatory or contractual basis.

revenue_lines.name: rPET pellets (fibre & non-food packaging grade)
revenue_lines.source: A-01 (capacity x utilisation ramp: pilot 1,500 t + Line 1 6,000 t from Q4 2027 + Line 2 to 12,000 t from mid-2029), A-02 (60% pellet mix), A-03 (ASP €1,250/t vs NWE food-grade rPET ~€1,350-1,440/t and vPET €1,000-1,100/t, S-07), A-05/A-06/A-07 (feedstock €250/t, yield 76%, conversion €300/t)

revenue_lines.name: rPET flakes
revenue_lines.source: A-01, A-02 (40% flake mix), A-04 (ASP €950/t, in line with NWE rPET flake €950-990/t, S-07), A-05/A-06/A-08 (flakes skip extrusion/SSP: conversion €210/t)

opex_lines.source: A-10 (hall sized for 12,000 t/yr from day one; lease terms T-04)

tax.notes: Dutch corporate income tax headline rate 25.8% (19% on first €200k ignored — simplification, A-29). Opening tax losses assumed equal to accumulated losses at 31 Dec 2026 (A-33); Dutch loss offset is limited to 50% of taxable profit above €1m per year — the model ignores this timing limit (disclosed).
